segments: and so that peace might be confirmed.
And the king prepared an agreeable {OCR?} place on the sea,
and in light boats they met one another,
and they confirmed complete love.
And when the Romans had rest from the West,
they set their faces toward the East.
And they went forth in the year 1252 [of the Greeks],
to all that region,
and went on.
And in that same year, 329
of the Arabs [940/941 AD]:
the sufferings of al-Radi, king of the Arabs, increased,
and he was completely unable to take care of himself.
And Sinan the physician, son of Thabit, laboured greatly with him,
and no treatment availed anything.
For he had a Turkish eunuch servant,
whose name was Zirak (Zirak
Irik):
the one who was in authority over everything of his;
and in this same year he fell sick and died.
And that king was swallowed up in great distress,
and he ordered, and four hundred jars of old, prime wine were poured out into the river Tigris.
And after a little while, he also died.
After al-Radi, al-Muttaqi, son of al-Muqtadir, [reigned] three years and one month.
In that same year, 329
of the Arabs, when he began to reign,
there was a great dearness [of prices] in Baghdad.
A kor of wheat was sold for one hundred and thirty gold dinars.
And people ate fruit and grass.
And there was again a great pestilence,
such that baskets of dead people were buried in a single grave without prayer.
And the river Tigris overflowed,
and destroyed many courtyards, palm trees, and other things.
And in the year 1253
of the Greeks [941/942 AD]:
the Romans again entered the territory of Cilicia,
and took captive from the district of Khammush fifteen
thousand people,
and burned the villages and departed.
And the famine grew severe in Baghdad,
and a kor of wheat was sold for two hundred and ten gold dinars,
and it even reached three hundred and seventeen gold dinars.
And people ate dead corpses.
And the bridge in Baghdad was broken,
and many people drowned in the Tigris.
And a year later, the Romans reached as far as Mayperqat, Arzan, and Nisibis,
and took many people captive,
and burned the villages and departed.
And in the year 331
of the Arabs [942/943 AD]:
the king of the Romans sent an envoy to al-Muttaqi, king of the Arabs,
demanding the Mandylion which was in the church of Edessa,
that which our Lord passed over His face
and His likeness was depicted upon it,
and sent it
